blocks.text: This chapter introduces the fundamental concepts of computer networks and explains how devices communicate with each other. Students learn about network architecture, key components, and the basic working of networks. It covers network models and layers, particularly the OSI model, along with different network topologies and types. The chapter also explains common networking devices such as NICs, switches, routers, modems, and wireless access points.

Students are introduced to essential protocols and services like TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP, and DNS, as well as concepts of IP addressing, IPv4/IPv6, subnetting, and NAT. They learn how to set up and configure home networks, including wired and wireless connections, and understand Wi-Fi security and encryption. The use of network diagnostic tools such as ping and ipconfig is also discussed. Finally, the chapter highlights network performance, security measures, and real-world practices to ensure safe and efficient communication.

A computer network allows different devices to connect and communicate with each other. It helps in sharing information quickly and easily. Communication through networks saves time and effort. Computer networks are used in homes, schools, offices, and businesses. Modern life depends heavily on computer networks for daily tasks.

blocks.caption: Figure 1.1: A computer network connects multiple devices to share data and resources (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.1).

blocks.text: Networks can connect computers, mobile phones, printers, and other digital devices (as shown in Figure 1.1). These devices communicate using cables or wireless signals. A network allows data, files, and resources to move from one device to another. Networks can be small or large depending on the need.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Networks support online learning and remote work. Businesses rely on networks for daily operations.

Internet browsing is a common example of network use. Mobile phones use networks for calls, messages, and apps. Schools use networks for online classes and learning systems. Banks use networks for online transactions and ATMs. Social media platforms work through computer networks. Smart homes also use networks to control devices.
